coverage.evidence: No secret is added, and two ways one could leak are closed. Both checkout steps in pr-checks.yml now set persist-credentials: false, so the job token no longer sits in .git/config where an uploaded artifact could carry it out - zizmor's artipacked finding, which it reported twice and now passes. The one project secret, FORBIDDEN_TERMS, is unchanged and read by name only, and the guard that reads it prints positions rather than matches. The new secrets job runs gitleaks with --redact.

Everything the new workflow fetches travels over TLS and is verified after arrival: osv-scanner over https from GitHub releases then checked against sha256 ca69b3d3..., gitleaks likewise against 551f6fc8..., zizmor and Semgrep pulled by image digest, Semgrep's rules fetched at commit 07135b52. Nothing is fetched by a mutable reference. The product itself still calls nothing.

coverage.reason: No TLS configuration exists to review: the product is an undeployed static bundle, TLS is terminated by whichever CDN eventually serves it, and Peer AI wrote no TLS job precisely because the config declares no environment with a URL. It becomes reviewable when hosting is chosen, issue #113.

coverage.evidence: The only secret is a GitHub Actions repository secret, replaceable in the settings with no code change since the workflow reads it by name. GH_TOKEN is minted per job and expires with it. The change adds no long-lived credential; it removes one from .git/config in two jobs.

The new workflow declares permissions: {} at the top level, so each job starts with nothing, and each of the four grants itself only contents: read. pr-checks.yml declares contents: read. No job can write to the repository, create a release or comment on a pull request. Least privilege is the default here rather than an exception.

Nothing is exposed that was not. The repository is public deliberately under PolyForm Noncommercial, recorded in CONTEXT.md's repo rules; there is no network service to leave open, since the product is a static bundle with no server and ADR-013's blob store does not exist yet. Scan output goes to the job log of a public repository, which is why gitleaks runs redacted.

Changes still reach main only through a pull request, and this change adds four more checks in front of that: secrets, dependencies, workflows and code. npm run ci:premerge must still print ALLOWED, and it treats anything not a pass - including a skipped job - as blocking, whatever the base branch. Branch protection remains off, #112, which is why that script exists.

coverage.reason: There is one environment, production, and nothing deployed to it. docs/02-architecture.md records no staging, no per-environment build and no runtime environment variable. Nothing to keep apart, which is also why Peer AI wrote no TLS or running-app job.

coverage.evidence: Real data cannot reach development or test, and the repo-rules job enforces it on every pull request: every figure in fixtures, tests and screenshots comes from the invented docs/seed-data.md, per repo rule 2, and the owner's own figures live only in their browser. This change touches no data and adds a scan that would report a leaked credential rather than a figure.

coverage.reason: There is no production to have access to: no server, no database, no hosting account in use. The question returns with hosting, #113, and ADR-013 shrinks it to a store of ciphertext nobody operating it can read.
OPS-04 applies from production, and there is no staging environment because there is no production environment to mirror - a deliberate absence recorded in the architecture rather than an oversight.

Nothing server-side holds data to back up. The owner's data lives on their device and its backup is the export file, with a nudge on unexported changes per D12. That is product behaviour, already built, not infrastructure.

No restore path or redundancy exists to test, for the same reason as OPS-05, and no uptime target has ever been recorded - stated as not recorded in the architecture rather than assumed. Import is the restore path and it is tested as a round-trip, M3.

summary: Pass. The change adds four CI checks and tightens the two that existed: permissions: {} at the top of the new workflow with contents: read per job, every tool pinned by checksum, digest or commit, four unpinned actions pinned, and the job credential no longer persisted in two checkouts. Seven of thirteen rules do not apply because there is no server, no second environment and nothing deployed.
